title: Preface
summary: A declassified 1950s CIA-era memo from the Chief of the Inspection and Security Staff to the Director of Central Intelligence requests approval and fund authorization for Project Bluebird, submitted directly due to its extreme sensitivity and covert nature rather than through the Projects Review Committee. It argues that various Agency interests in this program area should be consolidated into one project under controls to avoid compromise, and lists concurrences and approval markings. The OCR text is heavily garbled, so other details are unclear.

title: PROJECT BLUEBIRD
summary: Project Bluebird, an operational support proposal (March 1st agreement among ADOSO, ADOPC, ADOSI, and Chief I&SS) to establish immediate interrogation teams using polygraph, drugs, and hypnotism for defector/agent vetting and intelligence collection. Each three-person team comprises a psychiatrist, polygraph-hypnotist, and technician; two teams are proposed, with a Washington office cover for training. Covers operational control by a board, Top Secret security restrictions, personnel control under I&SS, training, field support, and a budget of about $65,515 for one year (itemized in Attachment A: personnel, supplies, equipment, transport, rent).

Coordination goes through key officers and contact officials in Army, Navy and Air Force, who limit further dissemination to need-to-know personnel tracked on a control list. Offices must report briefed personnel for that list. Also includes a transmittal slip, a project status note on security and a possible overseas operation, and an Inspection & Security Staff signature block (Col. Sheffield/Edwards). summary: A 1952 CIA memorandum sets security rules for Project BLUEBIRD documents: all classified TOP SECRET on an Eyes Only basis, handcarried between offices, some documents classified to hide true purpose, contact officers in Army, Navy, Air Force, and FBI, and a controlled access list maintained by I&SO. A second 20 May 1952 memo from the Deputy Security Officer concurs with a Staff Study on special interrogations (Project ARTICHOKE) and assigns I&SO responsibility pending a six-month review.

title: GNEEED SlaTES GOVERNMENT
summary: A 20 May 1952 memo from the Deputy Security Officer/CIA to the Assistant Director, Scientific Intelligence, concurring with the 15 May 1952 Staff Study on special interrogations (Project ARTICHOKE) to the DD/CI. It says the office will assume responsibilities upon approval, with a review meeting after six months to decide whether I&SO or another office should permanently conduct the project. Also includes a May 1950 record of a meeting on Project Bluebird, agreeing that OSI would collect information from U.S. government sources on speech-inducing drugs, narco-analysis and hypnotism, and Soviet/satellite trials involving drugs or interrogation, with later steps to divide collection fields among agencies. Much of the OCR text is garbled and partly illegible.

title: Forges onic
summary: A 1950 memo on Project Bluebird: a meeting among CIA/OSI and Defense representatives agreed to collect U.S. government information on speech-inducing drugs, hypnosis, interrogation techniques, and Soviet/satellite trials using drugs or special interrogation. A collection program would screen agencies for relevant information. Steps include dividing collection fields, possible unconventional warfare estimates, and referral to the Secretary of Defense. Dated April 1990 to the DCI. Text is largely OCR-garbled.

title: Approved
summary: A memorandum from the Assistant Deputy for Inspection and Security, addressed to AD/CSI, sets special handling rules for Project BLUEBIRD documents because the information is extremely sensitive. Requirements: CIA documents are hand-carried between offices, classified SECRET and marked "Eyes Only"; some documents may be classified SECRET, since a subject line does not reveal the program's purpose; key officers and contact points are to be arranged in Army, Navy and Air Force departments; documents sent from CIA to those departments go on a "Calls only" basis to contact officials, who must limit further dissemination to persons with need-to-know; a control list of briefed personnel is maintained by T&S and each office, for coordination and clearance. Signed by Colonel, GS3C.
